axis: Where a book's individuality lives: in an object, a place, or a surface.

directions.name: The Pressed Emblem
directions.thesis: A library of objects: every book is one thing you can hold.
commits: One drawn thing per book, cheap to hold in memory
trades: No atmosphere; a few stories, like Larra's, lack an obvious object
directions.rightWhen: Right when the shelf needs to read fast, not linger.

dna.anchor: Penguin Great Ideas / Pelican, cut paper
dna.ground: One ground tone per book, picked from its story, never by hash
dna.device: Single emblem, 2 to 3 tones, upper two thirds; ground text zone below y 232
dna.type: Fraunces 300 title, tracked uppercase author, mono level stamp, as Cover.tsx renders today
dna.cost: Cheapest to hold in memory: one considered object per book, 40 emblems total

directions.allTheWay: Every shelf becomes a cabinet of forty small held things.

books.title: The Tell-Tale Heart
books.author: Edgar Allan Poe
books.why: The pale, clouded eye isolates the narrator’s obsession against the slate darkness of the old man’s room.

books.title: La Parure
books.author: Guy de Maupassant
books.why: A brilliant borrowed necklace sits on the peach of imagined ballroom finery, embodying the luxury that becomes ruinous debt.

books.title: Don Quijote y los molinos
books.author: Miguel de Cervantes
books.why: The unmistakable windmill stands on the sand of La Mancha, ready to become a giant in Quijote’s imagination.

books.title: Dorothy and the Cyclone
books.author: L. Frank Baum
books.why: A broad storm twists into a narrow funnel over a teal storm sky, recalling the cyclone that lifts Dorothy out of Kansas.

books.title: Le Petit Chaperon rouge
books.author: Charles Perrault
books.motif: red hood beside grey wolf ear
books.why: The little red hood with a wolf's ear already rising behind it tells the whole tale, on a deep teal ground like the dark forest path to grandmother's house.

books.title: 三个成语故事
books.author: Traditional

books.why: The snake given useless feet is 画蛇添足, the best-known of the idiom fables — its inky "added" feet show the ruin of a finished thing, on a warm peach ground like an old storybook page.

books.title: O jabuti e a onça
books.author: Sílvio Romero
books.why: The bone flute identifies the tortoise’s ingenious trick, while the sage ground places it in the Brazilian forest.

books.title: Vuelva usted mañana
books.author: Mariano José de Larra
books.why: A motionless office clock rests on the marker ground of aging paperwork, turning bureaucratic delay into the story’s single emblem.

directions.name: The Mise-en-scène
directions.thesis: Every book is a place and a weather.
commits: Atmosphere, era and weather in a glance
One clear stage and one actor per scene
trades: Busiest direction at 104px; 40 scenes is the most authoring of the three
directions.rightWhen: Right when opening a book should feel like arriving somewhere.

dna.anchor: Folio Society flat-scene jackets, Charley Harper geometry
dna.ground: No separate ground tone; the horizon line is the ground
dna.device: Full-bleed flat scene, 4 tones, horizon or stage, one actor; solid text band y 250 to 330
dna.type: Fraunces 300 title set on the solid band, mono level stamp, small caps author
dna.cost: Most authoring: 40 distinct scenes, each needing its own weather and stage

directions.allTheWay: The shelf becomes forty small windows onto forty places.

books.title: The Tell-Tale Heart
books.author: Edgar Allan Poe
books.why: A brick-red heart interrupts the floorboards of a room pierced by midnight light, with an ink ground embodying the narrator’s concealed crime.

books.title: La Parure
books.author: Guy de Maupassant
books.why: An oversized necklace hangs against a ballroom’s evening teal, while the peach ground evokes the borrowed luxury of Mathilde’s one glorious night.

books.title: Don Quijote y los molinos
books.author: Miguel de Cervantes
books.why: A tiny mounted knight confronts three enormous windmills at brick-red dusk, with a sand ground recalling the dry plains of La Mancha.

books.title: Dorothy and the Cyclone
books.author: L. Frank Baum
books.why: A pale farmhouse tilts inside a descending geometric funnel, with a slate ground turning the Kansas afternoon into storm-darkness.

books.title: Le Petit Chaperon rouge
books.author: Charles Perrault
books.why: A solitary red hood enters a narrowing path beneath dark branches, with a forest-green ground establishing the still, threatening woodland afternoon.

books.title: 三个成语故事
books.author: Traditional
books.why: A farmer waits beside a stump in an untended field—a reading of 守株待兔—with the warm marker ground suggesting the long, dry afternoon of his foolish vigil.

books.title: O jabuti e a onça
books.author: Sílvio Romero
books.why: A small tortoise occupies a riverbank beneath a jaguar-shaped shadow, with the teal ground evoking shaded Brazilian water in the humid afternoon.

directions.name: The Endpaper
directions.thesis: A shelf of cloth spines: every book has its own woven pattern.
commits: Individuality at scale; works for abstract and CJK titles alike
Cheapest to author: one motif tiled, not one scene composed
trades: Motif reads as plain texture at 104px; the label shape repeats on every book
directions.rightWhen: Right when 40 books need to ship fast without looking hashed.

dna.ground: Motif tile repeated full bleed; no separate ground layer beneath it
dna.device: One motif tile, 2 to 3 tones, repeated full bleed; paper label x 24 to 196, y 210 to 300
dna.type: Fraunces 300 title on the label, ink text only; the label is always the light tone
dna.cost: Cheapest to author: one tile pattern per book, no scene composition

directions.allTheWay: The shelf reads as a run of forty bound cloth spines.
